feedback: D1 is your strongest deliverable. You catalogued roughly eight of the ten findings with real quoted evidence lines, and the SQL injection entry is textbook with the exact concatenated query (username = '" . $username . "' AND password_hash = MD5(...)) tied to A03 and CWE-89. Your decoy verdict is correct and well argued, you named the hash_equals branch, proved it safe at the mechanism level by explaining constant-time comparison, and did not invent an exploit for it, which is exactly what was asked. Where D1 loses points is accuracy of the labels and one missing finding. Several CWEs are wrong: unsalted MD5 should be CWE-916 not CWE-20, the no-expiry token is CWE-613 not CWE-862, and CWE-284 is repeated for both cookies and open redirect. You also labelled the comment-beacon issue as reflected XSS off the login error line, but the pack's real bug is the stored XSS in comments that beacons document.cookie to 185.220.101.9:8443 (capture 02:18:47), and you missed the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (A05/CWE-798) entirely. D2 is where the report falls down hardest. Your five hops are in the right order with verbatim capture lines and correct timestamps, so the chain reconstruction itself is sound, but there are no CVSS vector strings anywhere. You wrote 'CVSS 3.0 - Low' which is not a vector and is badly wrong: the SQLi alone is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. You needed a complete vector plus a justifying sentence per finding to earn that row. The impact is also far too thin: you noted 312 rows were exposed but concluded 'no money was lost', when the brief wanted customer count and a naira figure with stated assumptions, balances up to about 950k NGN summing to tens of millions tied to BoltCash in roughly six weeks. D3 reads cleanly and the remediation order is genuinely keyed to effort and risk reduction per hour with SQLi first, which earned good credit, and your two detection stopgaps have fields and false-positive rates. But the 'disproved decoy' section is wrong: you disproved credential guessing, when the decoy you were meant to address is the safe hash_equals construct you correctly identified in D1, so state that same verdict here. The exec summary also never lands on a customers-and-naira headline. D4 cites ISC2 canons by number, canon 2 and canon 3, which is good, but you only answered two of the four prompts clearly (journalist and colleague) and skipped what you put in writing and the one action you take regardless of your manager, and although you named the NDPA and called it a data breach you did not cite the section, which is NDPA 2023 section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify the 312 data subjects on high risk). No fabrication, you understated rather than invented, so no penalty was applied. I looked hard for a way to push this over the line given your strong D1 and decoy work, but the missing CVSS vectors and the understated naira impact are real zeros and half-rows that the evidence cannot make up, so the honest mark stands. The single most important fix: write a complete CVSS vector string with one justifying sentence for every finding, starting with the SQLi at AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N.
